A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RA-RAG work. All 25 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison; relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V2 reports original QA benchmark results, ablations, computational-efficiency measurements and real-world source-reliability evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains those original empirical evaluations and additionally reports 1,000-source results and wall-clock measurements for inference and reliability estimation.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same iterative reliability estimation, AlignScore filtering, semantic clustering, weighted majority voting and κ-RRSS procedure. Algorithm 1 is unchanged. Clarifications about deployment phases and response sets do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both use NQ, TriviaQA and single-hop HotpotQA with the same closed-ended QA requirements, synthetic reliability distributions and three real-world sources. Increasing the synthetic source count to 1,000 changes experimental scale within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Accuracy-comparison baselines are retained. The new runtime comparison in v3 Table A5 evaluates Vanilla RAG and Self-RAG against RA-RAG, extending comparator participation in efficiency evaluation beyond v2's comparison of RA-RAG with and without κ-RRSS.

E3.justification: The efficiency and relevance-selection comparisons replace their 20-source condition with 1,000 sources. Appendix K adds wall-clock evaluation of inference and reliability estimation under the NQ Beta-prior setting. Existing accuracy metrics, query splits, retrieval counts and κ remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 extends the κ-RRSS efficiency and relevance ablations to 1,000 sources and adds analysis separating inference latency from reliability-estimation overhead. The filtering, threshold-sensitivity, κ-sensitivity and qualitative analyses are retained, although several move within the document.

E5.justification: Both report averaging over 10 random trials and retain the same correlation significance reporting and plotted uncertainty. V3 introduces no new seed information, confidence intervals or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: V2's 20-source cost and selection-accuracy entries are replaced by 1,000-source results. V3 reports 5,415 tokens and 0.768 accuracy with κ-RRSS at 1,000 sources, versus 0.780 accuracy without selection. New Tables A5–A6 report 1.82 seconds per inference task and 14.81 hours for reliability estimation at that scale. These are newly reported conditions; matched benchmark, filtering and real-world results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The voting equations, reliability update and selection algorithm retain their mathematical substance. V3's explicit disjoint-cluster notation and clarification that Mκ contains responses spell out the existing construction; no substantive new assumption, derivation, theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the robustness, scalability and real-world applicability claims. However, Section 2 removes v2's explicit claim that RA-RAG is the first approach integrating source-reliability estimation into RAG, replacing it with a descriptive contribution statement.

C2.justification: V3 adds the specific failure condition that a previously reliable source could suddenly spread substantial misinformation after account compromise. Appendix K also interprets estimation overhead as practical preprocessing and discusses parallelization. The limitations concerning specialized topics and offline reliability updates were already present in v2.

D1.justification: V3 specifies a single RTX 6000 Ada GPU for runtime measurements, reports component timings and newly states that real-world reliability augmentation uses random sampling. Conversely, it removes the detailed counterfactual-context generation prompt in v2 Figure 14 while retaining the other prompts and corpus-construction description.

R1.justification: V3 removes the Xie et al. (2024) citation and reference, withdraws the explicit first-approach claim, and revises the comparison with Pan et al. (2024) around obscure reputations and the distinction between reputation and reliability. General RAG related work is retained in Appendix D.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: general related work and filtering analyses move to appendices, limitations become a separate section, and threshold studies move to the appendix's end. The overview section and Impact Statement are removed. Most retained prose remains similar, with local clarifications and an additional author.

P2.justification: V3 changes the page format, typography, headers and caption placement, and converts appendix prose from one column to two, extensively relocating and resizing displays. V2's overview diagram and counterfactual-context prompt figure disappear; v3 adds two runtime tables. Retained benchmark plots preserve their graphical content.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens the existing scalability argument with 1,000-source accuracy/cost results and measurements exposing both inference latency and upfront reliability-estimation costs. It also adds a concrete source-compromise limitation. These provide a limited net improvement, although removing the counterfactual-context prompt weakens benchmark reproducibility and the runtime experiment does not clearly identify its language-model configuration.
